verdict.reasoning: Patient states she became short of breath over the last hour while sitting watching TV: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and confirms this is while at rest watching TV.

Patient reports onset over the last hour while watching TV: "I was watching TV and just, like, over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and confirms this was while sitting: "This is while you're sitting watching tv?" "Yeah."

New onset is confirmed by no prior episodes: "have you noticed anything like this before?" "No." Not clearly worsening is supported by: "And this shortness of breath you're having, is it getting worse?" "No."
Patient describes palpitations: "I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going." and doctor clarifies: "so you're feeling your heart more than normal?" "Yeah."
Cough since yesterday and non-productive: "So I started with a cough yesterday" and to sputum: "Have you brought anything up?" "No, I haven't. No."
No chest pain is documented: "And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?" "No."
Chest soreness on deep breath is documented: "How about when you take a very deep breath in?" Patient: "I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore..."
C‑section scar tenderness is reported: "yeah, my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender."
No prior similar SOB episodes: "have you noticed anything like this before?" "No."

Four weeks postpartum s/p C‑section and baby well at home: "I had a C section a few weeks ago." "How long ago was that?" "Yeah. Four weeks." and "And are you with baby at the moment?" "Yes, I am." "how is baby doing?" "Yep, he's good."
Denies other medical problems: "apart from the C section and the shortness of breath. Have you got any other medical problems I should know about?" "No."
Codeine use pattern: "They gave me some codeine." "I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week."
Allergy and unknown reaction: "And are you allergic?" Doctor: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though." "And what happens when you take ibuprofen?" "I don't know."
Maternal history of leg clots: "my mum's had clots in her legs before, so I guess, you know. Yeah, that makes sense." This is consistent with leg DVT.
Partner at work: "Is anyone else with you at home?" "No, my partner's at work."
Timed pulse check: patient counts 30 beats; clinician calls it slightly fast. "How many did you count?" "I counted 30." "So your heart is running slightly fast at the moment."
No formal vitals or physical exam or diagnostic tests are obtained; only a home pulse count is done. The transcript includes no BP, temp, SpO2, auscultation, labs, imaging, or ECG.

Clinician expresses concern for clots/PE in a 4‑week postpartum C‑section patient with acute SOB: "Given that you've had a C section and you're short of breath, which has come on quite recently and quite quickly, it might be worth you going into the hospital..." and later: "what I'm worried about at the moment is, given that you've had a C section, some people can suffer with clots, and those can either be found in the legs or...your chest. So in your lungs."

Associations are all stated: one‑day dry cough ("I started with a cough yesterday" and "Have you brought anything up?" "No"), pleuritic-like chest soreness with deep breath ("when you take a very deep breath in?... yeah, my chest feels sore"), palpitations ("my heart is really going"), and no chest pain ("does it cause any pain in your chest?" "No.").

C‑section scar tenderness is acknowledged: patient reports tenderness and clinician links it with pain: "so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender." and later: "which is probably because of your shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under."
The clinician records and treats ibuprofen allergy as a diagnosis: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though." The reaction is not clarified, but allergy is clearly accepted.

Urgent ED evaluation now: "it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further" and later: "So I think that's the best thing to do for the time being" and "go fairly quickly."

Ambulance offered and declined; patient will self‑transport with baby: "I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself to the hospital with baby. Which one would you prefer?" Patient: "It feels a bit dramatic to call an ambulance. I'll go. I'll take myself." and doctor: "go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time."
Avoid codeine until assessed: "if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being."

Education on postpartum VTE risk and treatment, and patient agreement: "given that you've had a C section, some people can suffer with clots...in your lungs." "It's quite a common thing to happen, and it's not something to worry about, but needs to be checked out in the hospital first." "if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot." and patient: "my mum's had clots in her legs before... I know what they are." then when asked if she had questions: "No, no, I'm fine. I'll just take myself to the hospital."

The transcript notes C‑section scar tenderness but does not document advice to monitor the incision or defer changes to analgesia beyond "if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being." Monitoring the incision and deferring broader analgesia changes are not mentioned.

Follow‑up is through immediate ED evaluation: the plan is for her to go to the hospital now—"it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further" and emphasis to go "fairly quickly."
